description: We are a creative and multidisciplinary team of three students from TED Bodrum College, combining technology, data, design, and storytelling. We bring together skills in web development, AI, data analysis, creative writing, illustration, and visual design. We are passionate about turning complex space-related ideas into engaging and meaningful experiences. We aim to tell the story of forgotten lunar and Martian equipment through creativity, research, and innovative digital solutions.
summary:
Our project is an interactive, story-driven digital platform that introduces children to the stories of the spacecraft and equipment NASA has left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

The story follows Maysa, a young girl who discovers six mysterious postcards from her grandfather. Each postcard is connected to a real NASA space mission and an exploration vehicle or piece of equipment left behind. To uncover their stories, users must solve a series of puzzles, ranging from Braille and Morse code to Caesar cipher and geometric challenges. Along the way, they discover how these technologies were designed, what purposes they served, and how they contributed to our understanding of space.

Rather than presenting these objects as forgotten remains, our project portrays them as lasting traces of humanity’s curiosity, courage, and scientific progress. By combining storytelling, visual design, and problem-solving, we aim to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and meaningful for younger generations, inspiring them to see every discovery as the beginning of another journey.
details:
The Seventh Star is an interactive, story-driven digital platform that introduces children to the stories of past space missions and the spacecraft and equipment left behind through a combination of storytelling, puzzles, and visual exploration.

The experience begins with Maysa, a young girl whose grandfather dedicated his life to following the journeys of spacecraft travelling into the unknown. During a space mission, her grandfather mysteriously disappears, and Maysa receives no news from him for ten years. One day, a mysterious package arrives at her door. Inside, she finds six postcards, carefully tied together with a faded blue ribbon. Each postcard tells the story of a different space mission and invites Maysa to discover what the spacecraft explored, what they left behind, and why their journeys still matter. This narrative introduces users to the interactive experience, where they must solve a series of puzzles to uncover each postcard.

The six postcards feature Opportunity, Sojourner, Spirit, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Voyager 1, and Pioneer 10. Each one is unlocked by solving a different type of puzzle, including Braille, dominoes, Morse code, Caesar cipher, flower cipher, and geometric cipher. Users can access hints whenever they need guidance and retry their answers until they solve each challenge. Through this process, they learn about real space missions while actively participating in the discovery.

Every completed postcard reveals a new piece of a larger illustration. As users progress through all six missions, the pieces gradually come together to form a complete image, which they can print as a keepsake of their journey. After completing the six challenges, users discover a seventh and final postcard, written by Maysa herself. Its accompanying illustration shows Maysa wearing an astronaut suit and waving at her grandfather, who is represented as a star in the sky. This final scene gives the project its name, The Seventh Star, and brings the story to an emotional conclusion.

Beyond the interactive story, our website includes a Sources page featuring information about the spacecraft and direct links to relevant official NASA websites. This allows users to explore the scientific background of each mission and access reliable information beyond the platform. An About Us page also introduces our three team members and explains the responsibilities each person undertook during the project.

Our goal is to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and meaningful for younger audiences. By combining scientific information with storytelling, visual design, and interactive challenges, we aim to encourage curiosity about space while supporting logical thinking, problem-solving, and independent learning. We also want children to understand that when a spacecraft’s mission comes to an end, its contribution to science does not disappear. The objects left behind are lasting traces of humanity’s curiosity and determination to explore the unknown.

All written content, postcard stories, puzzles, and illustrations were created by our team members. We used Lovable to support the development of our website. Throughout the process, we considered scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, intuitive navigation, visual consistency, and the balance between educational value and entertainment. Our creative approach turns the history of space exploration into a personal journey, allowing users not only to learn about past missions but also to become part of the story themselves.
